messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert - sustained 5xx surge on /v1/complete (us-west-2). alert_id=INC-1905-XYZ - paging primary oncall

alice (oncall): acked. opening bridge and grabbing recent errors. seeing TLS handshake failures + 502s on a subset of nodes.

alice (oncall): quick probe -> some nodes are hitting container restart loops, OOMKilled then back, looks like autoscaler cycling. can someone from runtime confirm recent scheduler changes?

nina (eng-runtime): we rolled a scheduler tweak 30m ago to tighten binpacking for GPU memory. rolling windows show two pods in the left-most AZ with steady restart_count > 3. fetching kube events.

derek (sre): joining. can you paste a failed container log id? need sample request id for customer impact analysis.

alice (oncall): sample req id: c-19a7f. logs: "runtime: eviction threshold hit, cannot allocate buffer, terminating process". also seeing increased GC and ephemeral spike.

elena (eng-ml): that eviction message smells like quant-kernel memory growth when sequence lengths spike. do we have a recent change to max_seq_len or tokenization?

nina (eng-runtime): no token changes. scheduler tweak changes pod placement density which could increase memory pressure on siblings. might be a placement-induced OOM.

alice (oncall): mitigation attempt: cordon the noisy AZ and shift 30% of traffic to standby region (us-west-1). applying now.

ops-runbook-bot: runbook "az-eviction-containment" executed - steps: 1) cordon target AZ, 2) increase PodAntiAffinity, 3) scale up standby pool by 2 nodes.

alice (oncall): traffic shift in effect. error-rate dropped from 14% to 3.8% overall. p95 latency slightly higher for rerouted sessions.

harry (product): do we have customer-visible failures? incidence count? we need to decide on comms.

alice (oncall): initial count: ~7 customer sessions experienced mid-request errors; no persisted data loss. important to flag enterprise customers who might be impacted.

derek (sre): I'll track post-incident items. urgent: revert scheduler tweak or adjust pod memory requests. nina - can you revert canary cluster change?

nina (eng-runtime): initiating canary revert now (INF-3901). will run canary 10% and monitor.

alice (oncall): handoff note for next oncall in 40m: cordon still in place, traffic steering active, canary revert in progress. watch container restarts, GC time, and 5xx%.

incident-bot: bridge created - link: https://meet/incident/1905001234

nina (eng-runtime): canary report after 12m -> stable. restart_count back to normal on canary nodes. planning staged roll back across AZs.

alice (oncall): staged rollback started. removing cordon as nodes stabilize; lowering reroute gradually.

ops-runbook-bot: revert complete. cluster stabilized. scaled standby pool down.

alice (oncall): monitoring 30m post-revert. metrics show normal 5xx baseline. setting incident to mitigated.

harry (product): please schedule postmortem. include customer impact summary and a comms draft. propose 1 week from today, 15:00 PST.

derek (sre): scheduling postmortem for Thu 15:00 PST (one week). agenda: timeline, root cause (placement-induced memory pressure), why runbooks didn't trigger earlier, short & long term fixes, action owners.

elena (eng-ml): suggested technical actions to include: add a long-tail tokenization test to CI, add kernel memory regression checks, and add a preflight that simulates uneven AZ packing.

nina (eng-runtime): my immediate follow-ups: INF-3901 (revert and canary verification) - owner: nina - due: 1 day; INF-3902 (adjust pod memory requests + anti-affinity defaults) - owner: nina - due: 3 days.

derek (sre): SRE items: INF-3903 (alert rewrite) - add temporal smoothing and QPS threshold so short bursts don't P1-page - owner: derek - due: 2 days; INF-3904 (oncall playbook update) - add AZ cordon steps & comms template - owner: derek/ops - due: 5 days.

alice (oncall): ops note: we should avoid paging P1 for infra churn that doesn't affect >1% customer error unless QPS>500. propose new paging rule: page P1 if (customer-facing 5xx% >1 AND QPS>500) OR (5xx% >10 for >10m).

derek (sre): that read looks reasonable. I'll open INF-3903 with the exact boolean and add a doc linking to SLO owners.

harry (product): I'll prepare the external status: short note highlighting that mitigation prevented wider customer impact, list of affected customers (ops to confirm), and promise of a formal postmortem. will coordinate with legal if necessary. INF-3905 assigned to harry.

elena (eng-ml): long-term model-safety idea: implement an automatic fallback to a lower-memory model variant when node memory is constrained. INF-3906 - owner: eng-ml - due: 14 days.

nina (eng-runtime): also adding INF-3907: telemetry - emit per-process RSS histogram and eviction-count metric; makes failure mode observable without relying on logs. owner: runtime infra - due: 4 days.

alice (oncall): please pre-assign owners in the postmortem doc so action items don't get lost. i'd also like a follow-up check-in 2 weeks after postmortem to ensure closure.

derek (sre): will add a closure verification step to each INF ticket and link them in the postmortem doc.

ops-runbook-bot: incident log saved. severity P1 -> mitigated. postmortem scheduled. recommended review window: 7 days.

alice (oncall): thanks everyone. good mitigation work. reactions: :thumbsup: :coffee:

final note: keep using this thread for async updates; update INF tickets and the postmortem doc with any findings before the meeting.
